extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer-review researchers, peer-review trainers, and anyone assessing the quality of individual peer-review reports
extracted.subtask_description: Scoring the quality of a single peer-review report using the 7-item Review Quality Instrument (RQI): seven Likert-scaled dimensions covering coverage of the manuscript and review quality, aggregated to a mean score. Used as an outcome measure in peer-review research and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer discuss the importance of the research question?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–5 (1 = not at all, 5 = to a great extent). Evaluators should look for explicit comments on why the research question matters (clinical/public health/scientific relevance) rather than merely restating it. Lack of discussion lowers the item score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer discuss the originality of the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–5. Guidance includes noting whether the reviewer places the study in context of existing literature and comments on novelty or incremental contribution. Vague or absent remarks about novelty receive lower scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and weaknesses of the method
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer comment substantively on the methodology?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–5. Assess whether the reviewer identifies methodological strengths and limitations, discusses design, bias, analysis, sample size, and appropriateness of methods. Superficial statements like 'method is wrong' without explanation should be scored low unless substantiated (see substantiation item).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation (writing, organisation, clarity, tables/figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer comment on presentation quality (writing, organisation, clarity, tables/figures)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–5. Look for specific comments about clarity of prose, structure, readability, and quality/appropriateness of tables and figures. The instrument notes reviewers commonly neglect presentation; absence of such comments lowers the score for this item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer evaluate whether the conclusions follow from the data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–5. Evaluate whether the reviewer critiques the appropriateness of authors' inferences, whether alternative explanations are considered, and whether conclusions are overstated relative to results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructiveness of the comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Were the reviewer's comments constructive (i.e., would they help the authors improve the paper rather than merely criticising)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–5. Constructiveness is judged by presence of actionable suggestions, polite tone, and guidance for improvement. The RQI explicitly penalises reviews that only criticise without proposing how to fix issues; such reviews score lower on this item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiation of the comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Were the reviewer's comments substantiated with reasoning, evidence, or specific examples (rather than assertion)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–5. Look for explanation, citation, examples, or data supporting criticisms or praise. Assertions without reason (e.g., 'method is wrong' with no explanation) should be scored low on this item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate RQI score (mean of 7 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mean across the 7 items yields a continuous 1–5 quality score for an individual review (higher = higher-quality review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the arithmetic mean of the seven item scores to obtain an overall review quality score. The RQI was validated (Cronbach's alpha = 0.84) and has been used as the primary outcome in randomized trials of peer review interventions; treat the mean as a standardized, continuous outcome when comparing reviews or interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage across the five substantive dimensions (operational norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-quality review discusses every one of the five substantive dimensions rather than focusing on one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an implied expectation of the RQI: reviewers should address importance, originality, methods, presentation, and interpretation. Failure to cover multiple substantive dimensions indicates narrower, lower-quality reviews even if a single dimension is thorough.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructiveness expectation (operational norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who only criticise without proposing how to fix issues are rated lower on constructiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scoring constructiveness, value actionable, improvement-oriented feedback. Mere negative comments or dismissive statements reduce the constructiveness score; explicit suggested changes increase it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiation expectation (operational norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must supply reasons/evidence/examples for their criticisms; unsupported assertions lower scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operational norm reiterates the substantiation item: critiques should be accompanied by rationale, references, or concrete examples. Unsupported judgments should be penalised in scoring and in feedback to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to presentation (operational norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should comment on presentation (a dimension reviewers commonly neglect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scorers should check and reward specific feedback on writing, organisation, clarity, and figures/tables. Encouraging attention to presentation improves the comprehensiveness of reviews; lack of commentary here should be reflected in the presentation item score.
